source: DT-2026-06-07-planning-roadmap-materialization; user approved PRM planning ownership model and clarified no dogfood source special-cases.

loop_start.reason: Compiler loops start from CodeWiki source refs; agents may refresh context when chat is noisy, stale, or token-heavy.

validation.reason: Fresh validation is preferred; policy may require it for high-risk semantic gates.

next_loop.reason: The next compiler loop should start from CodeWiki source refs; the agent may refresh context when useful.

requirements.text: Decision compiler emits approved semantic decision_build evidence only; planning compiler owns roadmap decomposition and scheduling.
Planning compiler must materialize every executable accepted row/question into roadmap task/sprint/work-unit ownership, including blocked or last-in-queue work.
Planning compiler must support many-to-many row/task decomposition and only merge rows into one task when requirement ids and desired outcomes are compatible.
Planning compiler must reconcile existing roadmap and reorder queue/sprint waves by dependency, priority, conflict scopes, and agency budget for every accepted decision build.
Planning gate must block incomplete structured coverage; executable deferred work must still have durable roadmap ownership.
CodeWiki must not hard-code dogfood/self-hosting repository behavior; generic mechanisms must represent project-specific self-hosting context.

summary: Accepted planning-loop roadmap materialization and decomposition ownership decisions.

decision_table.title: Accepted planning-loop roadmap materialization and decomposition ownership decisions.

rows.question: PRM-000-DECISION-BUILD-BOUNDARY

state_delta.current: Decision and planning responsibilities can blur; previous wording implied planning might be decision-loop responsibility.
state_delta.desired: Decision loop owns semantic approval and accepted decision_build only: approved rows, requirements, KB mappings, propagation, risks, non-goals, downstream planning questions, and no roadmap mutation except decision evidence refs.

rows.proposed_change: Decision loop owns semantic approval and accepted decision_build only: approved rows, requirements, KB mappings, propagation, risks, non-goals, downstream planning questions, and no roadmap mutation except decision evidence refs.
rows.rationale: Keeps loop boundary clean: decision says what is approved; planning decides how work is organized.
rows.expected_outcome: Decision loop owns semantic approval and accepted decision_build only: approved rows, requirements, KB mappings, propagation, risks, non-goals, downstream planning questions, and no roadmap mutation except decision evidence refs.

rows.question: PRM-001-PLANNING-LOOP-DECOMPOSITION

state_delta.current: Planning may map rows once and stop, or treat deferral/build metadata as enough coverage for executable work.
state_delta.desired: Planning loop owns decomposition of every accepted executable decision row/question into sprints, atomic tasks, work units, dependencies, candidate files, conflict scopes, validation gates, and worker assignment metadata; planning loops until coverage is complete or routes back to decision.

rows.proposed_change: Planning loop owns decomposition of every accepted executable decision row/question into sprints, atomic tasks, work units, dependencies, candidate files, conflict scopes, validation gates, and worker assignment metadata; planning loops until coverage is complete or routes back to decision.
rows.rationale: Planning is the product core for turning decisions into efficient executable roadmap structure.
rows.expected_outcome: Planning loop owns decomposition of every accepted executable decision row/question into sprints, atomic tasks, work units, dependencies, candidate files, conflict scopes, validation gates, and worker assignment metadata; planning loops until coverage is complete or routes back to decision.

rows.question: PRM-002-ROADMAP-MATERIALIZATION-INVARIANT

state_delta.current: Executable accepted work can be represented only as a deferred trigger inside a planning build or sprint outcome.
state_delta.desired: Every accepted executable decision outcome gets durable roadmap materialization in the planning loop: task ids, sprint ids, and/or work-unit ids. If delayed, it remains visible as todo/blocked/replanned work with blocker/dependency/trigger and queue position, not build-only metadata.

rows.proposed_change: Every accepted executable decision outcome gets durable roadmap materialization in the planning loop: task ids, sprint ids, and/or work-unit ids. If delayed, it remains visible as todo/blocked/replanned work with blocker/dependency/trigger and queue position, not build-only metadata.
rows.rationale: Visible roadmap ownership prevents accepted work from disappearing behind open=0 or deferred prose.
rows.expected_outcome: Every accepted executable decision outcome gets durable roadmap materialization in the planning loop: task ids, sprint ids, and/or work-unit ids. If delayed, it remains visible as todo/blocked/replanned work with blocker/dependency/trigger and queue position, not build-only metadata.

rows.question: PRM-003-ROW-TASK-GRANULARITY

state_delta.current: A row can be mapped too broadly, or every row might be naively forced into one task even when split/merge is better.
state_delta.desired: Planning maps rows to atomic tasks using many-to-many coverage: one row may split into multiple tasks, several rows may share one task only when requirement ids/outcomes are compatible, and pure knowledge-only/no-op/already-implemented rows resolve with evidence instead of executable tasks.

rows.proposed_change: Planning maps rows to atomic tasks using many-to-many coverage: one row may split into multiple tasks, several rows may share one task only when requirement ids/outcomes are compatible, and pure knowledge-only/no-op/already-implemented rows resolve with evidence instead of executable tasks.
rows.rationale: Avoids both hidden residuals and inefficient task explosion.
rows.expected_outcome: Planning maps rows to atomic tasks using many-to-many coverage: one row may split into multiple tasks, several rows may share one task only when requirement ids/outcomes are compatible, and pure knowledge-only/no-op/already-implemented rows resolve with evidence instead of executable tasks.

rows.question: PRM-004-ROADMAP-REORDER-ON-PLANNING

state_delta.current: Roadmap order may not be systematically recomputed when accepted work enters planning.
state_delta.desired: Each planning loop that consumes an accepted decision_build reconciles active/closed roadmap, creates/refines/splits/supersedes tasks as needed, and reorders queue/sprint waves according to dependencies, priority, conflict scopes, and agency budget.

rows.proposed_change: Each planning loop that consumes an accepted decision_build reconciles active/closed roadmap, creates/refines/splits/supersedes tasks as needed, and reorders queue/sprint waves according to dependencies, priority, conflict scopes, and agency budget.
rows.rationale: New accepted work must be inserted deliberately, even if scheduled last.
rows.expected_outcome: Each planning loop that consumes an accepted decision_build reconciles active/closed roadmap, creates/refines/splits/supersedes tasks as needed, and reorders queue/sprint waves according to dependencies, priority, conflict scopes, and agency budget.

rows.question: PRM-005-PLANNING-GATE-COMPLETE-COVERAGE

state_delta.current: Planning gate can pass with partial coverage if deferrals or prose appear plausible.
state_delta.desired: Planning gate blocks until every accepted row/question has structured coverage: roadmap task/sprint/work-unit materialization, knowledge-only/no-work/already-implemented evidence, or explicit route-back blocker; executable deferred work must still have roadmap ownership.

rows.proposed_change: Planning gate blocks until every accepted row/question has structured coverage: roadmap task/sprint/work-unit materialization, knowledge-only/no-work/already-implemented evidence, or explicit route-back blocker; executable deferred work must still have roadmap ownership.
rows.rationale: Gate enforces the materialization invariant and protects against lost decisions.
rows.expected_outcome: Planning gate blocks until every accepted row/question has structured coverage: roadmap task/sprint/work-unit materialization, knowledge-only/no-work/already-implemented evidence, or explicit route-back blocker; executable deferred work must still have roadmap ownership.

rows.question: PRM-006-CURRENT-RESTRUCTURE-CORRECTION

state_delta.current: Accepted repo source-structure refactor is represented as DPA-012 sprint-owned replan trigger, not durable roadmap task/work-unit ownership after SPRINT-025.
state_delta.desired: Planning must add durable roadmap materialization for the accepted source-structure refactor now, ordered after SPRINT-025 repair work or blocked by it, then decompose into atomic migration sprint/tasks when blockers clear.

rows.proposed_change: Planning must add durable roadmap materialization for the accepted source-structure refactor now, ordered after SPRINT-025 repair work or blocked by it, then decompose into atomic migration sprint/tasks when blockers clear.
rows.rationale: This directly fixes the problem the user identified: accepted restructuring must be visible in roadmap even if scheduled last.
rows.expected_outcome: Planning must add durable roadmap materialization for the accepted source-structure refactor now, ordered after SPRINT-025 repair work or blocked by it, then decompose into atomic migration sprint/tasks when blockers clear.

rows.question: PRM-007-GENERIC-EXTENSION-NO-DOGFOOD-SPECIAL-CASE

state_delta.current: Dogfooding CodeWiki on the CodeWiki repository could tempt source behavior or schemas that special-case this project.
state_delta.desired: CodeWiki source remains generic for all Pi extension users. Self-hosting/dogfood details are represented as ordinary project configuration, roadmap/validation evidence, reload guidance, and runtime context—not hard-coded product behavior or CodeWiki-repo-specific schemas.

rows.proposed_change: CodeWiki source remains generic for all Pi extension users. Self-hosting/dogfood details are represented as ordinary project configuration, roadmap/validation evidence, reload guidance, and runtime context—not hard-coded product behavior or CodeWiki-repo-specific schemas.
rows.rationale: Product must be distributable and useful outside this repository while still supporting self-hosting through generic mechanisms.
rows.expected_outcome: CodeWiki source remains generic for all Pi extension users. Self-hosting/dogfood details are represented as ordinary project configuration, roadmap/validation evidence, reload guidance, and runtime context—not hard-coded product behavior or CodeWiki-repo-specific schemas.

accepted_decisions.summary: Decision loop owns semantic approval and accepted decision_build; planning owns roadmap decomposition and scheduling.
Planning loops until every accepted row/question has structured coverage or routes back to decision.
Executable accepted decisions must materialize in roadmap immediately as task/sprint/work-unit ownership, even when blocked or ordered last.
Planning uses many-to-many row/task mapping with compatible requirement IDs/outcomes as merge criteria.
Planning reconciles and reorders roadmap/sprint waves on every accepted decision build.
Planning gate blocks incomplete coverage and build-only executable deferrals.
Current repo source-structure refactor must become visible roadmap work now, after or blocked by SPRINT-025 repairs.
CodeWiki source remains generic; dogfood context uses generic config/roadmap/validation/runtime mechanisms only.
